searchText: I made an example wallet UI rethink based on 1559 principals. Thread here for more about the reasoning. https://twitter.com/JHancock/status/1408282853222146049?s=20 Anything ya'll would suggest here. <@!486501030046203915> <@!552133098075193354> <@!420951281910284289> I think the one slider is sufficient, but I may be missing something here. Ideal wallet: Just ask the user how much they are willing to pay for a fee. It doesn't matter what the current going rate is at all, only thing that matters is user's willingness to pay. So you mean remove the information about the Base Fee at all And only keep the slider. Remove basically everything about the fee and just ask "how much are you willing to pay". Not even a slider, because a slider has a max and a min. The slider's intent is to give the user an easy way to set "what they are willing to pay" The *right* question to ask the user is "how much are you willing to pay" *without* context. The context leads to cognitive bias and a wrong answer. without context, people will have no frame of reference. Yes, exactly. That is how the system works *best* for everyone. Giving users a frame of reference results in them making incorrect decisions. Because human brains are terrible. "How much are you willing to pay alone" Usually leads to their first question being "idk, how much do people normally pay." That is exactly what doesn't matter. Knowing that information causes your puny human brain to fall into an incorrect decision making trap. if they don't think it is urgent then don't they want to know if it is expected to be high or low now? depends on how much support you want to dedicate to answering why a transaction does not get through Does knowing the current base fee fit in there somewhere? <@!301186049323958275> "How much are you willing to pay?" "I don't know, how much are other people willing to pay?" "It doesn't matter. All that matters is how much *you* are willing to pay." "But then I have to make a decision." "Yeah, life is hard. This is good for you." hahahahaha The frame of, "how much are you willing to pay to X" FWIW, I can appreciate that both: A. this is probably too big of a paradigm shift for users and wallet developers. B. you are correct that humans *hate* making decisions. to get into the next block. To get in at all. The question is "how much are you willing to pay for this transaction to get included on the Ethereum blockchain" I mostly agree with you, but some context on "pay to what" I think needs some framing After the user answers, we can give them an inclusion timeline estimate. Guess this is baby steps then If they set a fee of $0.01 the wallet may tell them, "OK, we have queued up your transaction and sometime in the next 3-5 years we'll get you included. In the meantime, get a job so your willingness to pay increases and come back when you are willing to pay more." Given (B) here, I actually think the best UX is to simply not give any choices at all and just make an assertion to the user. "Your transaction will cost between $0.10 and $0.20." Decline. Accept. If we believe users *want* to make decisions, I think we should ask them the context-free question of willingness to pay. If we believe users don't want to make decisions, I think we should just assert the fee range to them. metamask pretty much does this atm Of course, there can be advanced options for adjusting this stuff. But I think the base UI should be one of those two. It gives you a price for contract interactions Updated 1559 wallet? Nah, the old system You could just give them a price and put the slider under advanced settings That would also work. Sure, I suppose your example could be an intermediate mode? Advanced mode gives fine control over every field, intermediate mode lets you adjust your max, basic mode just asserts the price to you. I would *prefer* intermediate mode just asked for a "willingness to pay" though rather than a with-context slider. yeah, that would fit even better probably I really do think that the context makes decision making worse. I'd use the slider, so I guess I am either intermediate or advanced XD (I do wish human brains weren't so terrible) it is what it is I guess i like binary decisions like this, they are not cognitively difficult but they also contextualise the choice, i don't think it'd be reasonable to ask people what their willingness to pay is, in a vacuum Because people are unreasonable? you could also play a round of "the price is right" : are you willing to pay this? yes, no -> ok then how about this? yes, no -> ok then, get a job :p In a land of spherical cows, "willingness to pay without context" results in the most accurate system. no, because the things they are paying for are intangible if i want an ice cream i know what it's worth and binary decisions are easy for human brains but here the price is just congestion, i don't know how much i care about something in these terms. do i want my payment to be successful? sure, but how much is that worth to me? no idea You have a desire to send some ETH to someone. Presumably it is possible to assert how much it is worth it to you to send that ETH, and beyond that number you will choose not to send the ETH. Why do you have no idea how much it is worth to you to transfer ETH? It is certainly a question that only you have enough context to answer. i don't even now if i'd denominate my answer in ETH 🙂 The UI can let you denominate in USD EUR or whatever, I think that is fine and useful. but i do see your point that the system as a whole works best with the data of what users are willing to pay (though that doesn't express their time preferences necessarily) binary seems like a nice tradeoff Time preference is tricky, and something we lack data on unfortunately. From a modeling perspective, I tend to assume it is a binary event. Included or not. but this is all a bit speculative, in a different world we'd do actual studies. we need more economists underpaying grad students to participate in lab experiments 🙂 Yes! The world just generally needs more underpaid ~~graduate students~~ people. 😬 😈 i also tend to think that things that are truly time sensitive will move to their own custom solutions, like cowswap or flashbots or others cool design <@!187490121698770945> in any case! i hope we see wallets experiment i'm also reminded of this post: https://billyrennekamp.medium.com/account-coordinator-a-proposal-for-the-future-of-wallets-9fc54032a202 1559 simplifies a lot of transaction management logic part of the wallet. in a sense it's a bit too bad that wallets today tend to be very monolithic. i'd want to be able to hack together a UX + bidding logic given 1559 simplifications without having to reimplement the whole account management, it would also favour experimentation Myetherwallet is adding me to a telegram group to talk with them more. Hopefully they experiment with something on ropsten so we can see things working! and, thanks! ❤️ If the max you are willing to pay is lower than the current fee will your transaction get rejected or can it linger until fees have come down and you get included? It will linger. Although if it is heavily underpriced it is likely to get forgotten (because clients have finite mempools).
